steps.instruction: Open the provisioned dashboard named 'Service health' (use search/dashboards to find it, e.g. via the Dashboards browse page or the search bar). Once it is displayed, report the exact titles of every panel on that dashboard, exactly as shown on screen, in order. Also report the dashboard's URL.

Create a NEW Grafana dashboard. Steps: from the Dashboards browse page click 'New' then 'New dashboard', choose 'Add visualization', and select the 'TestData DB' data source (a TestData data source). In the panel editor, change the panel type to 'Stat' (use the visualization type switcher at top-left of the editor). Set the panel's title to exactly: {{runid}} Availability. Make sure the query uses the TestData data source (e.g. scenario 'Random Walk' or the default). Click Apply. Then save the dashboard with the save button, and in the save dialog set the dashboard title to exactly: {{runid}} Bench Dashboard, then click Save. Verify the dashboard is saved (no unsaved-changes indicator, title shown in the top bar). Report the dashboard title, the panel title shown on the dashboard, and the page URL.

recorded.saved_confirmation: Dashboard saved (status alert in live DOM)

steps.instruction: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard', add a NEW Text panel. Steps: click the 'Add' button in the top toolbar and choose 'Visualization' (or use the dashboard menu > Add > Visualization), then in the panel editor switch the panel type to 'Text'. Set the panel title to exactly: {{runid}} Notes. In the text panel's content editor, enter markdown content that includes the runid, e.g.: Bench run {{runid}} — created for the dashboard build flow test. Then apply the panel (this build uses 'Back to dashboard' to apply) and SAVE the dashboard (click Save dashboard, confirm Save in the save dialog). Verify the save succeeded (a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation appears and there is no unsaved-changes indicator). Report the panel title shown on the dashboard, the text content visible in the panel, and whether the save confirmation appeared.

params.v4: Bench run {{runid}} — created for the dashboard build flow test.

steps.instruction: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard', do two things and make sure they are PERSISTED: (1) Add the tag '{{02-open.folder}}' to the dashboard: open dashboard settings via the gear/cog icon in the top bar, find the Tags field, add the tag '{{02-open.folder}}', and save the settings. (2) Set the dashboard time range to the last 6 hours AND persist it into the saved dashboard: open the time picker in the top bar, choose 'Last 6 hours' (or set from = now-6h, to = now), then click the Save dashboard button; in the save dialog TICK the checkbox 'Update default time range' before clicking Save. Verify a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation appears. Report: the tags now shown in dashboard settings (or on the dashboard), the time range shown in the top bar, whether the 'Update default time range' checkbox was ticked, and the save confirmation.

steps.instruction: On the currently open dashboard '{{runid}} Bench Dashboard', set the auto-refresh interval to 1 minute and PERSIST it. Steps: open the time picker in the top bar, find the 'Refresh interval' / 'Auto refresh' section, select '1m' (1 minute) as the refresh interval, and close the picker. Then click 'Save dashboard' and confirm Save in the dialog (tick 'Update default time range' if it is offered, to be safe). Verify a 'Dashboard saved' confirmation appears. Then do a full page reload of the dashboard URL WITHOUT time parameters (http://127.0.0.1:3000/d/{{03-create.url.p1}}/{{runid}}-bench-dashboard) and report what the top-bar time picker shows for the refresh interval after the reload (it should show '1m' or 'refreshing every 1m'), plus the time range shown. Report the refresh interval before and after the reload.
